findings.statement: Register an OAuth app by signing up for a Calendly developer account with GitHub or Google, then creating a new OAuth application (web or native), with no partner application or vetting step described.
findings.excerpt: Sign up for a Calendly developer account using your Github or Google account

mustContain: Sign up for a Calendly developer account

findings.statement: An OAuth app is created in one of two environments, Sandbox or Production; Calendly recommends starting in Sandbox and creating a second, separate app for Production when ready to use real customer data - no review step is described for that move.
findings.excerpt: We recommend starting with Sandbox for development and creating a second application for Production

findings.statement: All OAuth applications (web or native) use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with S256; the Production redirect URI must be HTTPS, while Sandbox allows HTTP on localhost.
findings.excerpt: use a specific redirect_uri, a Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE), and S256 for code_challenge_method

findings.statement: Calendly documents 23 OAuth scopes across six areas: Scheduling (availability, event types, locations, routing forms, scheduled events, scheduling links), User management (groups, organizations, users), Webhooks, Security & Compliance (activity log, data compliance, outgoing communications), Contacts, and Notetaker (meeting recaps).

Formally partnering with Calendly or getting listed through Calendly's own channels goes through a contact-based partner inquiry - submit information and a team member reaches out if there's a fit - separate from, and not required for, building and using your own OAuth app.
findings.excerpt: submit your information and a member of our team will reach out if there is a fit

findings.statement: Editing an existing OAuth app's name, kind, environment type, or redirect URI is self-serve, but the Client Secret and Webhook signing key are shown only once, at creation, and can't be retrieved again afterward.
findings.excerpt: you will not be able to access the Client Secret or Webhook signing key when editing

claim.text: Creating and using your own OAuth app is fully self-serve; Calendly's partner inquiry process is a separate, optional path for formal partnerships, not a requirement to build an integration.
Calendly's OAuth app creation and scopes docs describe no security review, questionnaire, or scan requirement of any kind.
No review step is described for creating an OAuth app, choosing scopes, or moving from Sandbox to Production.

tierReason.text: Calendly's OAuth docs describe a fully self-serve app-creation flow, with no review, security assessment, or partner requirement to build and use your own app against real customer data.

scopeForks.text: Formally partnering with Calendly (for example, to be listed as an official integration) goes through a separate, contact-based Partner Inquiry process with no published criteria or timeline - but this isn't required just to build and use your own OAuth app.

flow.text: A developer registers an OAuth app (Sandbox or Production), selects scopes, and users authorize it via Calendly's OAuth consent screen using PKCE.

appTypes.text: Sandbox and Production are separate app registrations; Calendly recommends building in Sandbox first, then creating a second app for Production with no review step in between.

tokenNotes.text: The Client Secret and Webhook signing key are shown only once, at app creation, and can't be retrieved again when editing the app afterward.

scopes.allows: Calendly groups its 23 scopes into six areas: Scheduling, User management, Webhooks, Security & Compliance, Contacts, and Notetaker.
scopes.neededFor: Picking which named scopes below your integration actually needs.

claim.text: Register an OAuth app by signing up for a Calendly developer account, then selecting scopes based on the data and functionality your app requires.

scopes.allows: Read, or update, user and event-type availability.
scopes.neededFor: Reading or managing when someone is bookable.

claim.text: availability:read reads user and event-type availability; availability:write updates event type availability.

scopes.allows: Read event type details and available times, or create/update event types.
scopes.neededFor: Reading or managing the meeting types someone offers.

claim.text: event_types:read reads event type details and available times; event_types:write creates or updates event types.

scopes.allows: Read scheduled events and invitee info, or create invitees, cancel events, and mark no-shows.
scopes.neededFor: Reading or managing actual booked meetings.

claim.text: scheduled_events:read reads scheduled events and invitee information; scheduled_events:write creates invitees, cancels events, and marks invitees as no-show.

scopes.neededFor: Looking up basic profile info for the authorizing user.

scopes.allows: Read organization data, memberships, and invitations, or invite/remove organization users.
scopes.neededFor: Org-wide integrations, not just a single user's own account.

claim.text: organizations:read reads organization data, memberships, and invitations; organizations:write invites or removes users from an organization.

scopes.allows: Read webhook subscriptions and sample payloads, or create/delete webhook subscriptions.
scopes.neededFor: Reacting to scheduling events in real time.

claim.text: webhooks:read reads webhook subscriptions and sample payloads; webhooks:write creates or deletes webhook subscriptions.

scopes.allows: Read contact details, or create/update/delete contacts.
scopes.neededFor: Syncing Calendly's contacts with another system.

claim.text: contacts:read reads contact details; contacts:write creates, updates, and deletes contacts.
data_compliance:write deletes invitee or event data.

scopes.allows: Read recap summaries, action items, discussions, and transcripts, or update/delete meeting recaps.
scopes.neededFor: Working with Calendly's AI meeting-notetaker output.

claim.text: meeting_recaps:read reads recap summaries, action items, discussions, and transcripts; meeting_recaps:write updates or deletes meeting recaps.

prerequisites.item: A Calendly developer account (sign up with GitHub or Google - separate from a regular Calendly user account)

claim.text: Registering an OAuth app requires a Calendly developer account, signed up via GitHub or Google, which is not the same as a regular Calendly user account.

prerequisites.item: A production-ready redirect URI (HTTPS required for Production; HTTP/localhost allowed only in Sandbox)

claim.text: The Production redirect URI must be HTTPS; Sandbox allows HTTP on localhost.

steps.title: Found Calendly's OAuth and scopes docs
steps.detail: The research stage located Calendly's OAuth app creation guide and its scopes reference.

claims.text: Calendly documents OAuth app creation and scopes at developer.calendly.com.

steps.title: Sign up for a Calendly developer account and create a Sandbox app
steps.detail: Separate from your regular Calendly login; start in Sandbox to build and test.

claims.text: A Calendly developer account (via GitHub or Google) is required to register an OAuth app.

steps.title: Select your scopes and implement PKCE
steps.detail: Choose from the 23 documented scopes; use PKCE with S256 for both web and native apps.

claims.text: Scopes are selected from Calendly's documented list, and PKCE with S256 is required for the authorization flow.

steps.title: Build and test against the Sandbox app
steps.detail: No review needed to build - the app works immediately for OAuth flows in Sandbox.

steps.title: Draft your scope justification
steps.detail: Use the Scope justification helper, in case you later pursue a formal Calendly partnership.

steps.title: Create a separate Production app and go live
steps.detail: No review step - create a second OAuth app registered for Production, with an HTTPS redirect URI, and switch your integration to it.

claims.text: Moving to Production means creating a second, separate OAuth app with an HTTPS redirect URI - no review step is described.

steps.title: Live - no Calendly review needed at any point
steps.detail: The integration works for real customer accounts as soon as the Production app is created.

provider.what: No review step is described anywhere in Calendly's OAuth documentation for creating an app, selecting scopes, or moving to Production.

claims.text: No review, security assessment, or partner requirement is described for building and using your own Calendly OAuth app.

customerAdmin.what: Calendly's docs don't describe an explicit admin-approval step for installing an OAuth app; org-level scopes like organizations:write likely still need the authorizing user to already hold admin permissions in their own Calendly organization, but this isn't spelled out as a separate gate.

endUser.who: The Calendly user authorizing the app
endUser.what: Grants authorization through Calendly's OAuth consent screen using PKCE.

claims.text: Users authorize the app through Calendly's OAuth consent screen, using the PKCE flow.

stuckPoints.reason: Lost the Client Secret or Webhook signing key
stuckPoints.fix: These are shown only once, at app creation. If lost, the only fix is creating a new OAuth app - editing an existing app never re-displays them.

claim.text: The Client Secret and Webhook signing key are shown only once, at creation, and can't be retrieved again when editing the app.

stuckPoints.reason: Production app rejects your redirect URI
stuckPoints.fix: Production requires an HTTPS redirect URI - the HTTP/localhost URIs allowed in Sandbox won't work once you switch to a Production app.

claim.text: For the Production environment, the redirect URI must be HTTPS; only Sandbox allows HTTP with a localhost domain.

whileYouWait.text: There's no review to wait on - a Sandbox app works immediately for development, and a Production app works immediately once created.

hardToUndo.text: The Client Secret and Webhook signing key can only be viewed once, at app creation - there's no way to retrieve them again later.
